hints: Compare the top nucleon numbers: $235+1$ on the left with $154+80$ from $\text{Nd}$ and $\text{Ge}$ on the right.
Compare the bottom proton numbers: $92$ on the left with $60+32$ on the right to see what charge x must carry.
Use the missing $2$ units of top number with zero missing bottom number to decide how many neutrons x must contain.
walkthrough: Identify the conserved quantities: top nucleon number $A$ and bottom proton number $Z$ must balance in the fission equation.
Total $A$ on the left is $235+1=236$. Total $A$ from the named products on the right is $154+80=234$.
The deficit on the right is $236-234=2$, so x must have total $A=2$.
Total $Z$ on the left is $92+0=92$. Total $Z$ from the named products is $60+32=92$, so x must have total $Z=0$.
A particle with $A=1$ and $Z=0$ is a neutron $^{1}_{0}\text{n}$. To get $A=2$ and $Z=0$, x must be two neutrons. This is option C.

options.A: One neutron would give total nucleon number $235$ on the right, not the $236$ required from $^{235}_{92}\text{U} + ^{1}_{0}\text{n}$.
options.B: Electrons have nucleon number $0$ and proton number $-1$, so they cannot supply the missing $2$ units of nucleon number and would change the charge balance.
options.C: Two $^{1}_{0}\text{n}$ add $2$ to the nucleon number and $0$ to the proton number, giving $154+80+2=236$ and $60+32+0=92$ as required.
options.D: Two protons would add $2$ to both nucleon number and proton number, making the right-side proton number $94$ instead of $92$.
